source_prompt:
# Instructions for accurately documenting failed brake tests in a vehicle inspection report

1. Start with the inspection records.
2.
completion:
Include the vehicle identification number (VIN), make, model, and year, along with the date and time of the inspection. Make sure to log the mileage of the vehicle as well.

3. Describe the testing process.
   - Identify the type of brake test performed (e.g., a decelerometer test, a roller brake test, a visual inspection, or a functionality test).
   - Detail how the test was conducted, including any equipment used and environmental conditions present at the time.

4. Record the results.
   - Note the initial observations such as any warning lights illuminated on the dashboard or noises coming from the braking system.
   - Document the test readings (if applicable) and identify which specific component or system failed (e.g., brake pads, rotors, brake lines, ABS system).
   - Discuss the quantifiable aspects of the failure, if available. For example, a decelerometer might record braking efficiency below the acceptable threshold.

5
